_about: Gemini 3.5 Flash drafted these answers (ungrounded) on 2 Nov 2026 from Abbas's context. Claude rewrote each one the same day, keeping the voice and structure but replacing every fact that conflicted with official pages or the board. 'fixed' lists what changed from Gemini's draft.

imperial-pres.tag: Round 1 has closed: round 2 on 11 Jan, and only with a supervisor
imperial-pres.lede: The Imperial College President's PhD Scholarships are the most prestigious doctoral funding Imperial offers. They're fully funded and a real route into world-class research. Round 1 closed on 2 Nov, so the live chance is round 2 on **11 Jan 2027**, and without a supervisor's agreement you're not ready for it.

us: A 3.5-year PhD pushes a US Match out to about 2031–32.
eu: Great for UK research networks, but it doesn't license you to practise.
interest: Public health, epidemiology and global health departments all sit here.

ul: **Full tuition fees** at the overseas rate.
**£27,036 a year** tax-free stipend for up to 3.5 years, plus **£2,000 a year** for research costs.
About **50 awards** a year, open to any nationality.
Your **$30,000 budget stays untouched**: it can go to USMLE fees and US clinical experience instead.
Any nationality, Bangladesh included.
A **first-class degree or equivalent**. How Imperial reads an MBBS comes down to your marks and class rank.
A **supervisor's agreement first**: find a faculty member in an area like the School of Public Health, email them your CV and a short proposal, and get their yes before you apply.
**Round 1: closed 2 Nov 2026** (decisions by 31 Jan 2027).
**Round 2: 11 Jan 2027.** Round 3: 1 Mar 2027.
Funded 2027–28 places can start as late as **1 Nov 2027**, which brushes against the end of your internship.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A PhD from Imperial in public health makes you exceptionally competitive for academic residency programmes, and London gives you a base for PLAB and NHS contacts. But the plan that works for 2029 is Step 1 during the internship, a paid US research job, then Step 2 CK. A 3.5-year PhD replaces that plan rather than adding to it, and your Match year moves to roughly 2031–32.

ul: **Catch 1: timing.** Round 1 has closed. Round 2 on 11 Jan 2027 is the realistic target, and you need an agreed supervisor before then.
**Catch 2: competition.** Fifty awards across the whole college, usually for people with research experience. A fresh MBBS with no publications needs a strong supervisor connection.
**Catch 3: years since graduation.** Many US programmes screen on how long ago you graduated. A PhD explains the gap well for academic programmes, less so for community ones.
**Catch 4: clinical distance.** Three and a half years in a research group means arranging observerships before you reapply to residency.

p: Treat this as a **physician-scientist route**, not a 2029 route. Apply in round 2 if a supervisor commits in the next two months. Otherwise keep your energy on Step 1 and a paid US research post.

fixed: Stipend: Gemini said £25,150 (2024/25). The current figure on the board is £27,036 a year.
Rounds: Gemini gave 4 Nov / 8 Jan / 13 Mar. The real rounds are 2 Nov 2026, 11 Jan 2027 and 1 Mar 2027.
Timeline: Gemini had you finishing the internship in late 2026. It runs from about Oct–Nov 2026 to late 2027, so the 1 Nov 2027 latest start matters.
Removed unverified claims about Imperial's space-agency links.
Round 1 wording: the original draft said Round 1 closes today. It closed on 2 Nov 2026, so the route now points to round 2 on 11 Jan 2027.

oist-phd.tag: Brilliant funding, wrong field for epidemiology
oist-phd.lede: OIST is an elite, English-language graduate university on Okinawa with one of the most generous PhD packages anywhere. It's basic science and computation rather than public health, so the question is whether you'd want a lab life for five years.

us: Five years in basic science puts a Match at about 2033.
eu: No help with licensing in the UK, Germany or Ireland.
interest: Neuroscience, genetics and computational biology yes; epidemiology no.

p: A single 5-year integrated PhD. The first two years are lab rotations and coursework, and the last three are thesis research. There are no departments: units cover molecular and cell biology, neuroscience, mathematics and computation, chemistry, physics and ecology.

ul: Tuition included, with a stipend of about **¥2.6 million a year**, rising to about ¥3.6 million.
Support for relocation and conference travel.
**Cost to apply: ¥5,000**, non-refundable and without waivers. It's small, but it isn't free.
Completion of a **bachelor's, master's or equivalent** before the admission date. Medicine isn't named, so confirm with admissions that an MBBS is accepted.
Check that your chosen unit actually has room to supervise new PhD students. OIST warns that strong applicants are rejected when the field has no space.
**15 Nov 2026, 23:59 JST** for the 2027 admissions workshop round.
Entry on 1 May or 1 Sep 2027, or **1 Jan 2028**. The January 2028 entry is the one that fits the end of your internship.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A PhD with strong papers helps for academic residencies, but US programmes weigh clinical experience and clinical research more heavily than bench work. Europe's licensing routes (PLAB, the German Kenntnisprüfung, Ireland's PRES) don't change at all.

ul: **Catch 1: timeline.** Starting in 2028 and finishing five years later puts a US Match at roughly 2033.
**Catch 2: field mismatch.** There is no public health or epidemiology unit. Computational biology is your closest door.
**Catch 3: admission.** Research experience matters a lot, and you'd be competing with people who have lab degrees.

p: Apply only if you're deliberately choosing a research career and would lean into computational work. For a Match-focused plan, skip it.

fixed: Application fee: Gemini said $0. OIST charges ¥5,000, non-refundable, no waivers (confirmed on oist.jp).
Stipend: Gemini said about ¥2.4 million; the board and OIST's package point to about ¥2.6 million.
Removed a second April application cycle and the GRE and acceptance-rate claims, none of which could be confirmed.
Timeline: Gemini had the internship ending in late 2026 or early 2027. It ends in late 2027, so the 1 Jan 2028 entry is the one that fits.

sanger-phd.tag: Exceptional if you can show genomics and coding skills
sanger-phd.lede: The Wellcome Sanger Institute 4-year PhD is one of the best-funded doctorates in the world, with a Cambridge degree at the end. It's a genomics and data-science programme, so it only works if that's the work you want.

us: Four years pushes a Match to about 2032.
eu: Strong UK academic standing; no licensing shortcut.
interest: Genomic epidemiology yes; policy, health economics and aerospace no.

p: A 1+3 model. In year one you do three short rotations in different labs plus taught modules, then choose your main project. The degree is awarded by the University of Cambridge, and you work on the Wellcome Genome Campus.

ul: **Full university tuition fees** and a stipend (£25,270 in year one at Oct 2025 rates).
Visa and NHS surcharge costs reimbursed.
At least **12 funded studentships**, whatever your nationality.
**Cost to apply:** nothing for the Sanger application. If selected, the Cambridge admission application costs **£20**.
Candidates expected to hold a **1st or good 2:1**, or an equivalent overseas qualification. Whether your MBBS is read that way is worth asking.
Genomics and data science are the focus. Basic Python or R and some statistics will help an MBBS profile a lot.
**24 Nov 2026, 09:00 GMT** is the closing time.
Start is in October 2027, which is likely to collide with your internship: ask whether a later start is possible before spending time on the application.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A Cambridge-linked PhD with strong genomics papers is a great physician-scientist credential and can put you in contact with US collaborators for letters. It doesn't give you US clinical experience, and a four-year PhD moves a Match to around 2032.

ul: **Catch 1: scope.** This is genomics and computation, not general public health.
**Catch 2: preparation.** Selection favours people with coding or lab skills you may not have built yet.
**Catch 3: clinical distance.** Four years away from patients means rebuilding clinical credibility afterwards.

p: If genomic epidemiology really pulls you, ask Sanger about starting later and whether an MBBS qualifies, and spend the internship building Python and R skills. If the 2029 Match is the priority, this isn't the route.

fixed: Deadline: Gemini said late November or early December. It's 24 Nov 2026 at 09:00 GMT.
Removed the IELTS 7.5 claim; check Cambridge's current language requirement for PhD entry.
Added the 1st / good 2:1 wording from Sanger's own page and the confirmed £20 Cambridge fee.
Timeline: Gemini treated October 2027 as the natural start. That sits on top of the internship, so ask Sanger about a later start.

eth-esop.tag: Fully funded, but not a road to a medical licence
eth-esop.lede: ETH Zurich's Excellence Scholarship (ESOP) pays for a Master's at one of Europe's top technical universities, with a real living allowance. It's a science degree, not a licence to practise, and the autumn start sits on top of your internship.

us: Prestige helps, but it adds years without US clinical experience.
eu: Doesn't unlock Swiss or EU medical licensing.
interest: Health Sciences & Technology and statistics fit; no MPH-style courses.

ul: **CHF 13,500 per semester** living allowance plus a tuition waiver.
About 60 awards, based on merit rather than financial need.
**Cost to apply: CHF 150** per programme (non-Swiss degree), non-refundable, no waivers. There's no extra ESOP fee.
Strong results in your degree, roughly the **top 10% of your class**.
A Master's application to ETH for the autumn semester, with a **thesis pre-proposal** you write yourself. That pre-proposal carries a lot of weight.
Typical English requirement is around IELTS 7.0 or TOEFL 100; check your programme's page.
The window is **1–30 Nov 2026**, with a September 2027 start. That start collides with the internship, so ask about a later one or plan for the next cycle.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: An ETH MSc in health sciences, statistics or biomedical engineering looks excellent on a residency application, and it links to aerospace physiology research. What it can't do is give you US clinical experience or any shortcut to practise in Switzerland or the EU, where you'd still need the local recognition exams and the language.

ul: **Catch 1: competition.** You need rank and a strong research idea, not just good marks.
**Catch 2: course fit.** ETH's health degrees are quantitative and molecular; there's no standard MPH.
**Catch 3: timeline.** One and a half to two years away from the USMLE track pushes a Match to about 2031.

p: Apply only if you want a quantitative research career and can write a convincing thesis pre-proposal. For a clinical Match, skip it. For European practice, Germany's Kenntnisprüfung or the UK's PLAB are more direct.

fixed: Living allowance: Gemini said CHF 12,000 per semester. The board has CHF 13,500.
Class rank: Gemini said top 10% in one answer and top 1–2% in another. ESOP's criterion is about the top 10%.
Application fee: Gemini said nothing; ETH charges CHF 150 per programme.
Timeline: Gemini had you finishing the internship in late 2026. It runs to late 2027, so the September 2027 start collides with it.

yenching.tag: Free, prestigious, but it's a China Studies degree
yenching.lede: The Yenching Academy at Peking University is a fully funded two-year Master's, often compared to a Rhodes or Marshall. It's an interdisciplinary China Studies degree, so it works as a global-health-policy credential rather than medical training.

us: A CV booster and a gap-explainer, with no clinical value.
eu: Helps global-health and policy careers, not licensing.
interest: Health policy via Society & Culture or Politics tracks; no epidemiology methods.

ul: Tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one round-trip fare and field-study costs.
No application fee is listed. Applying is free.
A bachelor's degree in any field, or someone currently enrolled and expecting a diploma by August of the intake year.
**English: IELTS 7.0 minimum.** Scores must be sent directly to the Academy.
Two academic letters from full or associate professors in your intended field, a personal statement (750 words) and a research-interest statement (up to 1,500 words).
**30 Nov 2026, 09:00 Beijing time.** Apply early: the closing hour is in the morning, China time.
The September 2027 start collides with your internship, so ask about arriving late or aim for the following year.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: It preserves your $30,000 and gives you a prestigious, well-explained one-to-two years after the MBBS. A thesis on China's health system, global health diplomacy or South Asia–East Asia comparisons would sit well with preventive-medicine programmes. It gives you no US clinical experience, and USMLE preparation will still need dedicated time.

ul: **Catch 1: degree type.** It's a Master of Arts in China Studies, not an MPH or epidemiology degree.
**Catch 2: workload.** Balancing the Academy with Step 1 and Step 2 CK is tough.
**Catch 3: no aerospace medicine.** There's no entry point here.

p: Worth applying if global health policy genuinely interests you and you can build a real thesis around it. If you want methods training, choose an epidemiology programme instead.

fixed: Deadline: Gemini said early December. It's 30 Nov 2026 at 09:00 Beijing time.
Research statement: Gemini said 750 words; the official limit is 1,500 words for the research-interest statement.
Removed an age limit of 28 that couldn't be confirmed on the official page.
Added the degree-timing rule and the sending-scores-directly requirement.

clarendon.tag: No form to fill, but your course choice matters
clarendon.lede: The Clarendon Fund is Oxford's flagship full-funding scheme. There's no separate application: you apply for your course, and strong applicants are considered automatically. That makes the course you choose, and when you can arrive, the real decision.

us: A one-year MSc is the only Oxford shape that keeps a 2030 Match realistic.
eu: UK base for PLAB and NHS contacts; no licence on its own.
interest: Global Health Science & Epidemiology is a direct fit.

ul: Full course fees plus a living grant for the whole degree.
A MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology carries overseas fees of about £36,900 (2027–28), so funding it yourself isn't realistic.
**Cost to apply: £75** for taught courses or **£20** for research courses. Applicants resident in a listed low-income country, Bangladesh included, can have it waived.
Any nationality, any subject. Medicine degrees are accepted.
The course deadline is what counts: everyone who applies by it and gets an offer is considered.
**Skip the MSc in International Health and Tropical Medicine:** it asks for 3+ years of low-resource work experience, which you don't have yet.
**1 Dec 2026, 12:00 UK** for the MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology. The Oxford and NDPH pages served older-cycle text on re-check, so confirm on the Graduate Admissions page.
An October 2027 start collides with the internship. The next realistic cycle is December 2027 for October 2028.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A one-year Oxford MSc in epidemiology is the strongest version of an academic credential you can get quickly, and Oxford's population-health groups have US collaborations that can lead to letters. It's still not US clinical experience, and in the UK it doesn't replace PLAB.

ul: **Catch 1: competition.** You can't apply to Clarendon directly. You need a place first, and marks and rank near the top.
**Catch 2: timing.** The cycle that fits your internship is next year's.
**Catch 3: exam clash.** An Oxford MSc plus Step 2 CK preparation in the same year is a heavy load.

p: Apply for the MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology only if you can get a later start or are happy to wait for the 2028 intake. Use the waiver, and never pay course fees from your $30,000.

fixed: Living stipend: Gemini quoted £18,622 (2024–25). That's out of date; the board lists the current award as full fees plus a living grant.
Deadline: Gemini said early January for medical sciences. The board lists 1 Dec 2026 for the Global Health MSc.
Application fee: Gemini said about £75. It's £75 for taught and £20 for research, with a waiver available for Bangladesh.
Gemini recommended the Tropical Medicine MSc; it needs 3+ years of experience, so it was removed. Removed an unverified count of awards.

emjm-neurasmus.tag: Funded and prestigious, but a neuroscience degree
emjm-neurasmus.lede: Neurasmus is a two-year Erasmus Mundus joint Master's in neuroscience that pays €1,400 a month. If you're excited by the brain, it's a great route into Europe. If you want population health, a different Erasmus programme fits you much better.

us: Basic-science research isn't what US residencies value most.
eu: A funded base in Europe, but it doesn't license you.
interest: Space neuroscience overlaps; epidemiology does not.

ul: The standard Erasmus Mundus package: **participation costs covered and €1,400 a month for up to 24 months**, plus insurance.
About 20 places from 800+ applicants.
The €4,500 per semester participation cost applies only to self-funded students.
No application fee was found in the official guidance.
A bachelor's-level degree (180 ECTS or equivalent), and medicine is a listed field.
No work-experience rule, though research experience helps.
IELTS around 6.5 to 7.0 is typical; check the call text.
Erasmus Mundus also limits how long you may have lived or worked in a programme country before you apply.
The scholarship call runs **1 Sep – 1 Dec 2026, 12:00 CET**. It's one of the 1 December group.
A September 2027 start collides with your internship: ask about late arrival, or aim for 2028.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A Master's with a good thesis boosts a neurology or neurosurgery application, and living in Germany or France gives you time to learn the language for later licensing. None of it counts as US clinical experience, and time on a two-year programme pushes a US Match out to 2030 or later.

ul: **Catch 1: field.** It's basic and translational neuroscience, not public health.
**Catch 2: competition.** Candidates with lab or coding experience have an edge.
**Catch 3: workload.** Two universities, lab rotations and USMLE preparation is a lot at once.

p: Apply only if neuroscience is a real interest. If epidemiology is the goal, put your motivation letter into Europubhealth+ or IDOH instead.

fixed: Deadline: Gemini said early December to mid-January. It's 1 Dec 2026 at 12:00.
Removed the €18,000 tuition and €3,000–€4,000 travel figures, which don't match the standard scholarship description, and the partner list, which couldn't be confirmed.
Timeline: Gemini had the internship ending in September 2027 and then a 2027 start; the internship actually runs to late 2027.

hkpfs.tag: Among the best fits for your timing, if you can match a PhD to your interests
hkpfs.lede: The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme pays a generous stipend with no nationality, age or work-experience limit, and it allows a deferred start to 31 January 2028. That deferral is why it fits your internship better than most.

us: A multi-year PhD moves a Match well past 2029.
eu: Strong academic credential; no licensing impact.
interest: HKU and CUHK public health schools are global leaders.

ul: **HK$344,400 a year** (about US$44,000) plus **HK$14,400 a year** for travel, for up to three years.
Host universities usually cover the tuition for fellows, but confirm that in your offer: it isn't part of the RGC award.
**Cost to apply:** the initial application is free. Each university's own application costs about **HK$500 per programme**.
Any nationality. No age or work-experience limit.
You choose up to **two programmes at one or two universities**.
You'll need a strong research proposal, references and English scores. The selection panel rates research potential, academic record and leadership.
**1 Dec 2026**: the initial application to the RGC closes at **12:00 noon Hong Kong time**, and university deadlines can follow almost immediately.
Fellows normally start Jul–Sep 2027, but with RGC approval you can defer to **31 January 2028**.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A PhD in infectious-disease epidemiology or public health from HKU or CUHK, with real publications, is a strong credential for academic residency programmes. It doesn't license you in the UK or Europe, and it doesn't replace US clinical experience.

ul: **Catch 1: timeline.** Even a deferred start leaves you several years from a US Match.
**Catch 2: competition.** About 400 fellowships worldwide, and the panel prizes publications.
**Catch 3: no aerospace medicine.** Hong Kong isn't a hub for it.

p: Submit the RGC step by noon on 1 Dec if you want a research career: it's one of the few big PhD schemes that works around an internship. Weigh it carefully against the 2029 plan first.

fixed: Stipend: Gemini quoted HK$331,200 and HK$13,800. The current amounts are HK$344,400 and HK$14,400.
Gemini said apply in December 2027 for a 2028 start. Apply now: the RGC allows deferral to 31 Jan 2028.
Universities: Gemini said up to two of eight universities; the RGC wording is up to two programmes at one or two universities.
Added the HK$500 per-programme university fee, and removed the acceptance-rate figures.

jhu-phd.tag: Strong funding; ask one question about work experience first
jhu-phd.lede: The Johns Hopkins Bloomberg PhD in Epidemiology is a fully funded, top-ranked programme, and it's one of the few US PhDs that explicitly says a prior graduate degree isn't required. The work-experience wording is still unresolved: the programme page lists one year of full-time experience, while the FAQ says it is only strongly recommended.

us: A 4–5 year PhD moves a US clinical Match to about 2032.
eu: Great for academic and global-health careers, no licensing impact.
interest: Epidemiology and clinical research are exactly this.

ul: A guaranteed minimum stipend of **$52,000 a year** through June 2027, plus tuition, fees and medical benefits, guaranteed for at least the first four years. The Epi FAQ adds 100% tuition for up to four years plus an NIH pre-doctoral level stipend.
Stipend rates beyond June 2027 depend on the union's successor agreement.
**Cost to apply: $155** through SOPHAS for the first programme, $65 for each additional. A limited number of waivers exist (Bangladesh residents qualify; request before submitting).
A prior graduate degree is 'not required, but highly recommended'. **GRE is not required and not reviewed.**

**Work experience:** the programme page lists one year of full-time work experience in a related field, but the Epi FAQ says a year of full-time post-baccalaureate work is 'strongly recommended'. Email BSPH.EpiAcademic@jh.edu to ask whether your internship counts.
**Three letters**, from professional or academic referees or a mix; the FAQ asks for at least one academic, advisor preferred.
A **statement of objectives and research goals**, with a two-page limit per the Epi FAQ.

**Credential evaluation is mandatory:** WES ICAP course-by-course ($239, ordered through SOPHAS) or ECE sent directly to Hopkins. **ECFMG is not accepted.** Even if the portal lists it as optional, it is required for international coursework.

**English minimums:** IELTS Academic 7, Duolingo 130, PTE Academic 68, or TOEFL iBT 100 for scores taken before 21 Jan 2026. A TOEFL taken on the new format needs **5.0** on the 1 to 6 scale. Scores must be under two years old.

**Waiver:** only through a WES or ECE evaluation showing English was the only language of instruction for a four-year bachelor's or professional degree, and only once that evaluation is received. Medium-of-instruction letters are not accepted.
**1 Dec 2026** via SOPHAS, for an August 2027 start. Submit by the deadline; supporting documents must be received within two weeks after.
WES takes weeks to start, so order it today.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A Hopkins epidemiology PhD builds US contacts, publications and letters, and can lead to physician-scientist tracks. It also takes four to five years, so a US clinical Match lands around 2032, and an August 2027 start collides with your internship.

ul: **Catch 1: admission.** One of the most competitive PhDs in the field. Most successful applicants have a master's or research track record.
**Catch 2: work experience.** The two Hopkins pages disagree and an internship may not count.
**Catch 3: timing.** August 2027 starts before your internship ends.
**Catch 4: years since graduation.** A PhD finishing around 2031–32 means your MBBS is six years old when you apply.

p: Email the department this week, quoting both work-experience lines. If they say the internship counts and allow a later start, apply. Otherwise, next year's cycle suits your timeline better.

fixed: Stipend: Gemini said $35,000–$40,000. Hopkins guarantees a minimum of $52,000 through June 2027.
Statement length: The notes said no limit was found; the Epi FAQ states a two-page limit on the statement of objectives and research goals.
English minimum: The notes said TOEFL 100; the official page says 100 applies to old-format scores, and a TOEFL taken after 21 Jan 2026 needs 5.0.
Work experience: The notes said one year is required; the programme page lists it as a requirement but the FAQ says strongly recommended, so email BSPH.EpiAcademic@jh.edu.
Letters, credential evaluation and GRE: Confirmed on the official page: three letters, WES ICAP or ECE (ECFMG not accepted), GRE not required or reviewed.
Removed the earlier claim that the SOPHAS fee is shared with Emory: Emory's PhD uses the Laney application, not SOPHAS.
jhu-phd.ai_note: Drafted from your uploaded notes, then checked against the official pages on 9 Nov 2026. Where they disagreed, the official page won.

emory-phd.tag: Fully funded and shares a deadline with Hopkins
emory-phd.lede: Emory's Rollins PhD in Epidemiology gives every admitted student full tuition and a stipend, sits next to the CDC, and shares the same 1 December deadline as Hopkins. It applies through the Laney Graduate School for **$75**, not SOPHAS. It's very competitive, and the same timing trade-off applies.

us: A 4–5 year PhD moves a clinical Match to about 2032–33.

ul: A full-tuition scholarship for all admitted PhD students plus a stipend of **$43,260 a year** (Laney, FY26–27 union rate). The Rollins programme page still says $42,000 for 2025–26, which is stale.
Health insurance support as part of the package.
**Cost to apply: $75** through the Laney Graduate School application. It is separate from SOPHAS, so it does not share the Hopkins fee.
A bachelor's is the stated minimum, so an MBBS qualifies. GRE is optional.
It's very selective: more than 200 applications for 10–14 places, and admitted students often hold advanced degrees.
**Three letters of recommendation**, from people familiar with your academic performance.
A **500-word statement of purpose**: previous research experience or training, research interests, how the programme addresses them, and long-term goals.
A **statement on building collaborative and respectful graduate communities** (500 words in the Laney application).
**Name at least two** Epidemiology graduate faculty you would like to work with.
**Unofficial transcripts** from each post-secondary institution, with a notarized translation if they are not in English. Official transcripts come only after admission.

**Credential evaluation:** the programme and Laney pages do not make it mandatory (Laney says international applicants 'may want to consider' it). But the Rollins general how-to-apply page says international applicants must use WES, and that page covers all degrees. Ask Epidemiology admissions before you decide.
**English:** TOEFL or IELTS for international applicants. No numeric minimum for Epidemiology was found on the official pages, so ask the programme.
**1 Dec 2026** is the final deadline for PhD applicants; Emory deadlines fall at midnight US Eastern.
Shortlisted applicants get a virtual visit day, most often a Friday in the first two weeks of February.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: An Emory PhD gives you CDC-adjacent networks and US letters. It's also several years on F-1 status before any Match, and your MBBS year of graduation ages meanwhile.

ul: **Catch 1: admission.** The competition is heavy for a first-time researcher.
**Catch 2: timing.** An August 2027 start doesn't fit the internship.
**Catch 3: clinical gap.** Five years without patient care.
**Catch 4: credential evaluation unclear.** The pages disagree on whether WES is needed, so ask early to avoid a surprise.

p: Apply only if you're committed to the research route and have an answer on start dates; this is a separate Laney application. If the 2029 Match is the priority, the paid US research job route is better.

fixed: Stipend: Gemini said $37,000–$40,000. The current Laney rate is $43,260 for FY26–27; the Rollins page still shows a stale $42,000.
Application fee: The notes said the fee was $155 through SOPHAS with a $65 saving if bundled with Hopkins; the official pages say Emory's fee is $75 through the Laney application.
Credential evaluation: The notes said none is needed; Laney does not require it, but the Rollins general page says international applicants must use WES, so ask.
English minimum: The notes found no number; no numeric Epidemiology minimum was found on the official pages either.
Statements: Confirmed on the official page: a 500-word statement of purpose and a communities statement, three letters, and at least two named faculty.
Timeline: Gemini had you applying in December 2027; the deadline is 1 Dec 2026, and August 2027 start dates clash with the internship.
emory-phd.ai_note: Drafted from your uploaded notes, then checked against the official pages on 9 Nov 2026. Where they disagreed, the official page won.

singa.tag: Good money, and the January 2028 intake suits you
singa.lede: A*STAR's SINGA PhD is fully funded, carries no service bond, and has a second intake in January 2028 that lines up with the end of your internship. It sits in science and engineering, so any health angle has to be biomedical or data-driven.

us: A 4-year PhD pushes a Match to about 2032.
eu: Academic standing only, no licensing impact.
interest: Biomedical and data angles only; no clinical track.

ul: Full tuition, plus **S$2,700 a month** (rising to S$3,200 after the qualifying exam).
A **S$1,000** settling-in allowance and **S$1,500** towards airfare.
No service bond.
No application fee is stated.
International graduates in science and engineering fields at NUS, NTU, SUTD or SMU, supervised through A*STAR.
Whether an MBBS counts for your chosen area depends on the host school: ask early.
**1 Dec 2026, 23:59 Singapore time** for the August 2027 intake.
**1 June 2027** for the **January 2028** intake: this is the one that fits your departure window.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A Singapore PhD builds strong biomedical or data skills, and the stipend lets you save money for USMLE costs. It's four years of non-clinical work, so a US Match moves to around 2032, and it does nothing for UK or European licensing.

ul: **Catch 1: field.** Bench science and computation, not epidemiology.
**Catch 2: no aerospace medicine.** There's no civilian track.

p: Treat Mayo as one target among many. Set job alerts now so you learn what fits, then apply widely to labs at other universities too. Do not wait on Mayo alone.

fixed: Salary: Gemini said $65,000-$80,000; the board's range for Mayo posts is about $67-79k, so the two roughly agree.
Aerospace medicine: Gemini said Mayo has a world-renowned aerospace research lab and a direct post for you; no current post found on the board matches that, and the claim couldn't be confirmed.
Start timing: Gemini said you can contact PIs during the internship before the degree is in hand; the official posts need the MBBS conferred, so you apply once it is.
Removed Gemini's claim that Mayo regularly hires Bangladeshi IMGs and that fellows publish 3-6 papers in 1-2 years, which couldn't be confirmed.
Portal: Gemini said to search jobs.mayoclinic.org; this matches the official portal.

ecfmg-j1rs.tag: Not a job: it is the visa paperwork once a US lab has offered you a post
ecfmg-j1rs.lede: ECFMG sponsors J-1 visas for physicians doing research at US hosts that have no J-1 designation of their own. It only starts after a lab offers you a post, so the hard part is the offer, not the visa. Fees are small: about **$750** for the first year.

us: Makes small US labs and hospitals able to hire you.
eu: A US visa has no value for European licensing.
interest: Opens public health and epidemiology research posts.

ul: **$370** ECFMG annual application fee (every year of sponsorship), **$220** SEVIS, and the J-1 visa fee, listed as **$160** on ECFMG's page.
Special appeals, only if needed: $367 (State Department) + $200 (ECFMG).
Minimum funding for the exchange visitor is **$1,600 a month**. ECFMG does not pay you; the host does.
You, with a US host that has offered a research post and is working with ECFMG. Your host's Training Program Liaison coordinates the application, and you apply through MyIntealth.
The board's card says USMLE and ECFMG certification are generally not required for this category; confirm with ECFMG.
Rolling, tied to the start date of the appointment. The $370 fee is annual.
Nothing to do until you hold an offer, which opens only after the MBBS is conferred.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: This is plumbing for the paid-research-post route, and it is the safest visa leg when the host cannot sponsor directly. It matters only for the US goal. A year on a J-1 research scholar visa builds the letters and research the Match looks for, but it does not count as clinical experience.

ul: **Catch 1: no offer, no sponsorship.** ECFMG does not find you a job.
**Catch 2: no patient care.** The board describes the category as research with no or incidental patient contact, so check what your host plans.
**Catch 3: the two-year home rule.** It may apply if US or Bangladeshi government funding is involved. Ask your host before accepting.
**Catch 4: fees recur and move.** The $370 repeats each year and the visa fee line should be re-checked before you pay.

p: Do not spend time here yet. Read the EVSP checklist once so nothing surprises you, then put the effort into getting offers. Budget about $750 for year one and ask each host whether they sponsor directly or through ECFMG.

fixed: Sponsorship fee: Gemini said about $1,800-$2,200; the official EVSP page lists a $370 annual application fee.
Visa fee: Gemini said a $205 DS-160 fee; ECFMG's page lists the J-1 visa application fee at $160, to be re-checked against the State Department's current fee. SEVIS $220 matches.
Pay floor: Gemini said hosts must pay the Department of State minimum of $55,000-$75,000; the official checklist sets a minimum of $1,600 a month for the exchange visitor.
Removed Gemini's claims about English-test requirements, $2,000-$4,000 insurance and 4-6 week DS-2019 times, which couldn't be confirmed on the pages checked.
Gemini's point that you need a host offer first matches the official page.

ecfmg.tag: The one step you fully control: about $3,360 and no US Match without it
ecfmg.lede: USMLE Steps 1 and 2 CK plus ECFMG certification are the gate to any US residency. Nobody awards you this, you sit and pay. The listed fees come to about **$3,360** before OET and prep, and the 2027 Pathways application closes **31 Jan 2027**.

interest: Step scores help research and preventive medicine applications.

ul: ECFMG certification application **$580**. Step 1 **$905** ($695 + $210 surcharge). Step 2 CK **$930** ($695 + $235). Pathway application **$945**.
That is **$3,360** in listed fees. OET Medicine, prep material, ERAS and the Match come on top.
All amounts are USD. Fees change each year and the April 2026 schedule applies to 2027.
Graduates of schools listed in WDOMS with an ECFMG sponsor note. Check your school's note on wdoms.org before paying for anything.
Register through FSMB for the exams and MyIntealth for certification.
Exams run all year in three-month eligibility periods, so there is no single exam deadline.
2027 Pathways close **31 Jan 2027**; the 2028 season is not announced.
The 2027 Match is too early for you. Target 2028 or 2029. Step 2 CK is the score screen.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: Everything in the US plan runs through this. For Europe it does nothing for licensing, though a strong Step 2 CK score still signals ability in an MPH or PhD application. With no licence, the board reads Pathway 6 (Mini-CEX) as the realistic clinical-skills option.

ul: **Catch 1: sponsor note.** If your school's WDOMS sponsor note does not cover your graduation year, check with ECFMG before you pay.
**Catch 2: new exam format.** The board notes Step 1 and Step 2 CK now use 30-minute blocks. Practise with the new tutorial.
**Catch 3: the stack grows.** Add OET, a prep resource, a clinical placement and the Match. Keep a running budget.
**Catch 4: rules move.** The board is tracking visa and J-1 policy changes. Re-read ECFMG news before each payment.

p: Start Step 1 preparation during the internship, since it is the one step entirely in your hands. Do not pay the Pathway fee until the 2028 season opens and you know which Match year you are targeting.

fixed: Exam fees: Gemini said Step 1 and Step 2 CK are about $1,200-$1,300 each; the official fees are $905 for Step 1 and $930 for Step 2 CK, including the overseas surcharge.
Exam cost total: Gemini said about $4,000-$5,000 for registrations; the listed official fees add to about $3,360, with OET priced separately and not verified.
Certification fee: Gemini left out the $580 ECFMG certification application fee that applies from 1 Apr 2026.
Pathway: Gemini said most fresh graduates use Pathway 3 or 4; the board reads Pathway 6 (Mini-CEX) as the realistic one without a licence.
Gemini's $945 Pathway fee and 31 Jan Pathways close match the official page.

maastricht-gh.tag: Funded and live, but the file is due 10 Dec 2026 and the Sept 2027 start clashes
maastricht-gh.lede: A one-year MSc in Global Health at Maastricht with the NL High Potential Scholarship (€1,550 a month). It is one of the few funded European master's routes the board found live. Your complete file is due **10 Dec 2026**, and the scholarship form closes **1 Feb 2027**.

us: Research skills and a funded year, but it delays the 2029 Match.
eu: A funded Dutch degree, though no licence.
interest: Global health is a direct match to your interests.

ul: **€1,550 a month**. The pages checked do not list what else is covered, so confirm on UM's scholarship page whether tuition, insurance and visa costs are waived.
The scholarship itself charges no fee. You pay a **€100** UM handling fee by 10 Dec 2026, and UM does not cover it.
Non-EU/EEA applicants admitted to the programme, with a **GPA of at least 7.5/10 (75%)** and aged **35 or under on 1 Sep 2027**. Only about 2% of applicants are awarded.
Per the board, how UM classifies an MBBS (bachelor's, which would need the GRE General, or bachelor's plus master's, which would not) is an open question. Ask UM admissions.

Complete programme file by **10 Dec 2026, 23:59 CET**. This is the gate for scholarship consideration, and it is five weeks away.
Scholarship form closes **1 Feb 2027, 23:59 CET**. General non-EU admission closes 1 May 2027.

p: One of the few funded European master's routes still live in the board's 1 Nov audit. It gives a Dutch degree, but no medical licence there. **Catch 3: competition.** About 2% of applicants win, and the award is not guaranteed even if admitted.
**Catch 4: timeline.** A one-year master's starting Sept 2027 collides with the internship and delays the 2029 Match.

us: Strongest research credential of the Maastricht pair, but it delays the 2029 Match.
eu: A funded Dutch degree, though no licence.
interest: Epidemiology is exactly your stated interest.

The scholarship itself charges no fee. You pay a **€100** UM handling fee by 10 Dec 2026, and UM does not cover it.

nih-vf.tag: Great letters if you get in, but it is unclear an MBBS counts as the doctorate
nih-vf.lede: NIH Visiting Fellows are paid research trainees placed lab by lab in NIH's intramural programme. There is no central application and no deadline. The open question is whether a Bangladeshi MBBS counts as the required doctoral degree.

us: NIH letters would be strong for the Match.
interest: Epidemiology and infectious disease labs fit well.

ul: A stipend scaled by experience. No official figure was verified.
No application fee stated. NIH sponsors your J-1; visa-stage government fees would apply.
A Visiting Fellow holds a doctoral degree with under five years of relevant postdoctoral experience. The board cites NIH policy as "PhD, MD or equivalent".
Whether your MBBS counts as MD-equivalent is not confirmed. Ask NIH's Division of International Services (DIS) before investing time.
No deadline. Labs fill posts when they have an opening.
You cannot start before your MBBS is conferred, so think 2027-28.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: If it works, it is among the best CV lines for a US residency application: recent US research, an NIH letter and a paid year. It does nothing for a European licence. It is also open-ended, with the whole process decided by one lab's budget.

ul: **Catch 1: eligibility is unconfirmed.** If NIH does not treat the MBBS as a doctoral degree, the route is closed.
**Catch 2: you do not apply to NIH centrally.** You apply to labs, and the lab chooses.
**Catch 3: no track record.** Fellows usually bring research experience; you have none yet.
**Catch 4: not clinical.** It does not count as US clinical experience.

p: Send one short email to DIS asking whether an MBBS qualifies. If yes, add NIH labs to the same outreach list as your other US posts. If no, you have lost nothing.

fixed: Eligibility: Gemini said your MBBS qualifies as a doctoral-level degree; the official requirement is a doctoral degree and whether a Bangladeshi MBBS counts is not confirmed.
Stipend: Gemini said $68,000-$75,000 a year; no stipend figure was verified and NIH scales it with experience.
Process: Gemini said the PI starts the process through OITE; the official route is that DIS processes the case after a lab selects the fellow, and you do not apply to DIS directly.
Gemini's point that there is no central deadline and NIH sponsors the J-1 matches the official pages.

emjm-all.tag: A real funded route, but only if you pick programmes that take MBBS
emjm-all.lede: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are EU-funded two-year degrees across several countries. This card stands for the whole catalogue, including 37 new programmes selected in July 2026. There is no central application: you apply to each consortium, up to three per cycle.

us: A funded research master's, but it pushes the 2029 Match to 2030 or later.
eu: A foothold in Europe and the language, though no licence.
interest: Public health, epidemiology and health data programmes exist.

ul: Scholarship holders pay no tuition and get a monthly allowance. The board's programme cards show about **€1,400 a month** for 24 months, with the exact terms set per programme.
Most programmes charge no application fee. This is not guaranteed, so check each site.
Anyone with a bachelor's-level degree that the programme accepts. MBBS is accepted for health programmes but not all, so read each requirement.
Apply to at most **three** programmes.
The EACEA page says most programmes take applications **between October and January** for the following September. Each consortium sets its own dates.
Individual cards on the board hold the exact dates for the programmes you are likely to pick.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: Choose public health, epidemiology, nutrition, health data science or tropical medicine. They add a European credential and base, but a two-year master's starting in Sept 2027 overlaps your internship and moves the US Match back. Choose a one-programme shortlist rather than a scattergun.

ul: **Catch 1: scholarship not guaranteed.** The catalogue warns that some listed programmes no longer offer Erasmus Mundus scholarships. Eu-HEM on this board is one.
**Catch 2: each programme is its own application.** Dates, documents and fees all differ.
**Catch 3: timeline.** A Sept 2027 start collides with the internship and delays the 2029 Match.
**Catch 4: no licence.** These are academic degrees, not routes to practise.

p: Use the catalogue to shortlist three programmes whose pages explicitly accept medicine, check each scholarship line, then apply to all three. Decide about the Sept 2027 clash only when you have an offer.

fixed: Deadlines: Gemini said deadlines generally fall between 15 Dec and mid-Feb; the EACEA page says most programmes take applications between October and January, with each consortium setting its own dates.
Opening dates: Gemini said applications open Oct-Nov; some programmes open later (imAGEin 6 Jan 2027, MemBioMed 1 Dec 2026).
Catalogue size: Gemini said over 150 programmes; the board scanned all 218 in the catalogue and 37 new ones were confirmed in July 2026.
Gemini's list of example programmes (Europubhealth+, PHDA, TROPMED, BIOETHICS) was not checked here, and the catalogue warns some programmes no longer offer scholarships.
Gemini's three-programme limit and "most have no application fee" match the official page.

usphd.tag: Fully funded, but 1 Dec deadlines are close and it delays the clinical Match
usphd.lede: Funded PhDs in epidemiology, biostatistics and informatics pay tuition and a stipend. Funded-PhD deadlines at schools of public health cluster on **1 Dec 2026**, four weeks away. By the end you would be well past graduation, which hurts a clinical Match but suits a research career.

us: Great research credential, but a 4-6 year PhD collides with the 2029 Match.
eu: Respected in Europe, no licensing value.
interest: Epidemiology and biostatistics are your stated interests.

ul: The funding comes from each university's own offer (tuition waiver plus stipend), not from SOPHAS. Terms differ per school, so read the offer.

Application fee: **$155** first programme, **$65** each extra. Bangladesh is on SOPHAS's Least Developed Countries list, so you can request the international fee waiver (limited and first-come; it covers the first $155 only, so apply before you submit).
An MBBS is usually accepted for direct entry. JHU Epidemiology needs TOEFL 100 (5.0 on the new TOEFL scale) or IELTS 7 and does not review the GRE. Harvard PHS requires the GRE.
UNC does not need the GRE; funding there is not guaranteed and files incomplete on 31 Jan are not reviewed.
**1 Dec 2026** for JHU and Harvard (Harvard 5 pm). **15 Dec 2026** for UNC. JHU's PhD in Clinical Investigation closes 1 Mar 2027.
No single deadline: each programme page is the authority.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A PhD is a research-career route, not a faster way to residency. Four to six years of non-clinical work leaves you seven to nine years past graduation at Match time. It can bring a visa, US mentors and strong letters, but you cannot do it and the 2029 Match together.

ul: **Catch 1: timing.** You would need test scores, three letters and a research statement within weeks.
**Catch 2: no research record.** Admissions committees expect evidence of research ability.
**Catch 3: Match conflict.** The PhD runs into the 2030s and weakens a clinical application.
**Catch 4: funding terms vary.** Department funding is not always guaranteed.

p: Apply only if you have genuinely decided that research matters more than the 2029 Match. If that is you, prepare JHU first, since it needs no GRE, and use the Bangladesh fee waiver. If the Match is the priority, skip it.

fixed: SOPHAS fee: Gemini said about $150 for the first school; the official fee is $155 first and $65 for each additional programme, with a fee waiver available for Bangladesh.
GRE: Gemini said Harvard, Johns Hopkins, UNC and Michigan have made the GRE optional; the board's read is that Harvard PHS requires it for all applicants while JHU and UNC do not.
Portal: Gemini said you apply to all these schools through SOPHAS; some, such as UNC Gillings' PhD, use their own graduate-school portal.
Deadlines: Gemini said 1-15 Dec for most programmes; verified dates are 1 Dec (JHU, Harvard 5 pm) and 15 Dec (UNC).
Removed Gemini's stipend range of $32,000-$48,000, which couldn't be confirmed.

kh.tag: Closed for the 2027 cohort; look again around June 2027 for the 2028 cohort
kh.lede: Knight-Hennessy Scholars funds a Stanford graduate degree. The 2027 cohort closed on **6 Oct 2026, 1:00 pm PT**. Nothing can be done this cycle. The next realistic cycle is the autumn 2028 cohort.

us: Superb for a research career, but not a route to residency.
interest: Fit depends on which Stanford programme you would apply to.

ul: KHS funds a Stanford graduate degree. Check the KHS site for the exact package, which was not re-verified here.
KHS charges **no application fee**. The Stanford programme application is **$125**.
You must be admitted to a Stanford graduate programme and also selected by KHS. Neither guarantees the other.
Your first bachelor's degree must have been received within the seven years before enrolment. A 2026 MBBS graduate qualifies, but the window is time-limited.
2027 cohort: opened 1 Jun 2026, **closed 6 Oct 2026**. The Stanford programme application was due by the earlier of its KHS deadline or 1 Dec 2026.
Next cohort (autumn 2028) would open about **1 Jun 2027** on the same annual pattern. This is not officially announced.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A funded Stanford degree is a strong signal, but it is academic, not clinical, and it does not change your Match timeline in your favour. The 2028 cohort fits after the internship, which is why it is worth keeping on the list.

ul: **Catch 1: closed.** Nothing can be submitted for 2027.
**Catch 2: two admissions.** Stanford can reject you even if KHS likes you.
**Catch 3: tiny acceptance.** KHS is highly selective; acceptance figures were not verified.
**Catch 4: leadership evidence.** KHS selects for leadership and civic engagement, which takes time to build.

p: Do not spend effort now. Use 2027 to build a leadership and research story, then check the KHS site in June 2027 for the 2028 cohort.

fixed: Deadline: Gemini said the KHS deadline was 8 Oct 2026, 1:00 pm PT; the official deadline was 6 Oct 2026, 1:00 pm PT, so the cycle is already closed.
Degree-recency rule: Gemini said the first bachelor's must be from 2020 or later; the official rule is within the seven years before enrolment, which a 2026 MBBS graduate meets.
Fee: Gemini mentioned no fee; KHS charges none and the separate Stanford application is $125.
Removed Gemini's stipend figure ($52,000+), $15,000 relocation allowance and selection statistics, which couldn't be confirmed.

emjm-hygieia.tag: MBBS is explicitly eligible, but the fee and 2027 deadline are not published yet
emjm-hygieia.lede: HYGIEIA is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's on health and wellbeing across the lifespan, run by Lusófona (Lisbon), Belgrade and the Balearic Islands. Medical sciences are explicitly eligible, so an MBBS fits. Only 25 students are taken per cohort, and the programme site did not state a 2027 deadline when checked.

us: Two years of non-clinical study that pushes the 2029 Match back.
eu: A European base and network; no licence.
interest: Prevention and public health focus matches your interest.

ul: Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders are exempt from tuition. The monthly amount is not stated on the pages checked, and the board shows it as not stated. Other Erasmus Mundus cards show about €1,400.
Application fee: not published.
A degree at EQF Level 6 in pharmaceutical or medical sciences, nutrition, sports, biochemistry, chemistry, biology or related health and life sciences. An MBBS fits.
An approved English test is mandatory even if your studies were in English (unless you are a native speaker). The cohort is 25 students, and only a minority are self-financed.
The 2027 deadline is **not published** on the programme site. The previous call ran from mid-Nov 2025 to mid-Feb 2026, so a similar window is likely.
The board lists a September 2027 start; the pages checked did not state one.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: Useful if you want a European public health base and are willing to delay the Match. A September 2027 start overlaps your internship and the two-year degree runs until mid-2029, so the 2029 Match would move to 2030 or later. It offers no US experience and no European licence.

ul: **Catch 1: dates unconfirmed.** Recheck hygieiamaster.eu every few weeks.
**Catch 2: tiny intake.** Twenty-five places in total, a minority self-funded.
**Catch 3: English test.** You must sit one even though your MBBS was taught in English.
**Catch 4: timeline.** Sept 2027 collides with the internship and the Match.

p: Keep it on a watch list and book an English test so you are not waiting on that. Apply only if you decide you want a European public health route over the 2029 Match.

fixed: Deadline: Gemini said applications open Oct-Nov and close 15 Jan 2027; the programme site had not published a 2027 date, and the last call ran mid-Nov to mid-Feb.
Consortium: Gemini said partners "typically" include Portugal, Spain, Italy and Poland; the official consortium is Lusófona (Lisbon), Belgrade and the Balearic Islands.

Stipend: Gemini said €1,400 a month; the programme site pages checked state no amount.
Intake size: Gemini called it less competitive than famous programmes; the official intake is only 25 students per cohort.

lshtm-fund.tag: One award a year, full tuition plus £22,000, but the 2027-28 round is unannounced
lshtm-fund.lede: The LSHTM Fund Scholarship covers full overseas tuition and a tax-free £22,000 stipend for a London-based MSc. Only **one** award is offered a year, and the 2027-28 round has not been published. The 2026-27 deadline was 4 Mar 2026.

us: A strong research credential, but a year away from the Match timeline.
eu: A UK degree and public health network.
interest: MSc Epidemiology is an excellent fit.

ul: Full overseas-rate tuition, including mandatory field trip fees, plus a tax-free stipend of **£22,000**.
You pay a £50 admissions fee. No separate scholarship fee is stated.

Nationals of, and resident in, World Bank low- and middle-income countries. Bangladesh is a World Bank lower-middle-income country, so you should qualify; confirm the exact wording on the 2027-28 page.

A first or upper-second-class degree (or equivalent), and an offer for a London-based intensive MSc. Joint programmes (Global Mental Health, Health Policy Planning and Financing, One Health, Veterinary Epidemiology) are excluded.
The 2027-28 deadline is **not published**. LSHTM adds 2027-28 adverts as funding becomes available.
For reference only, the 2026-27 deadline was **16:00 GMT, Wednesday 4 March 2026**, with both steps done by then.
LSHTM's general MSc closing date for 2027-28 entry is 25 Jul 2027.

sections.h: How it fits the US and Europe goals
p: A funded MSc Epidemiology at LSHTM gives research training, publications and a UK network. It does not give a UK licence and does not help the US Match timeline. A 2027 start collides with the internship, so the 2028-29 round is the realistic one.

ul: **Catch 1: one award.** A single scholarship across all LSHTM master's applicants.
**Catch 2: two steps.** The scholarship form only appears after you submit the MSc application.
**Catch 3: dates unknown.** Plan from last year's early-March deadline but wait for the 2027-28 page.
**Catch 4: timeline.** Starting in 2027 overlaps the internship and delays the Match.

p: Treat it as a lottery ticket for the 2028-29 round. Keep your application documents ready, watch the LSHTM scholarships page, and do not plan finances around it.

fixed: Fee: Gemini mentioned no application fee; LSHTM charges a £50 admissions fee that must be paid before the scholarship deadline.
Number of awards: Gemini described it as a premier award with no count; the official page says only one LSHTM Fund Scholarship is offered per year.

Gemini's £22,000 stipend and two-step process match the official page; the official page states the income-group rule rather than naming Bangladesh.

mext.tag: A clean fit after the internship, but a long process via the Ministry
mext.lede: The MEXT Research Student scholarship via the Embassy of Japan funds a master's or PhD in Japan. For Bangladesh the first step is the Ministry of Education's advert each April, then the Embassy. The round that fits you opens in **April 2027** for April 2028 arrival, which matches the end of your internship.

us: A multi-year degree in Japan that delays the 2029 Match.
interest: Public health and epidemiology research is available.
